On the precats thing, Toyota wanting it to be a ULEV, Ultra Low Emissions Vehicle, so they put precats in to further reduce emissions, because the precats start doing their thing immediately upon startup, whereas the catalytic converter takes a minute to warm up. Unfortunately, the matrix inside the manifold is made of a ceramic, and they tend to break down over time, and the dust/debris gets sucked into the engine and causes damage. So just about anyone who buys an MR2 Spyder/MRS guts them ASAP. My car is in several pieces covered in PB blaster at the moment so I can do it when parts come in next week. It's a fairly straightforward process, if a little challenging since the nuts are a real pain, but fingers crossed. Certainly beats my engine being toast at some point in the near future; I'm lucky as it is.

Oh, also, it's something you have to do yourself - gutting the precats or replacing the header with no precats is an illegal modification of the emissions control system, so generally no reputable shop will do it. But it doesn't seem to be a huge deal to DIY
